newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: GOVT OBSERVER TO ATTEND WIK SUMMIT
Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer say the Federal Government will take part in a summit organised by the Cape York Land Council on the implications of the High Court's Wik Decision.
The court found Native title could co-exist with pastoral leases.
The national summit examining the impact of the case will take place in Cairns next week on Wednesday and Thursday.
The Cape York Land Council invited industry and community groups to participate while Government has been invited to send an observer.
Mr Fischer says the Government has decided to send a representative from the Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet to the summit.
BORBIDGE SAYS NATIVE TITLE MUST BE RESOLVED

Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge says the native title issue is the most important facing the country, and he'll be asking the Prime Minister in Canberra on Monday to provide certainty for pastoral leaseholders.
Rob Borbidge says his latest advice is that up to 85 per cent of the state could be subject to native title claims.
He says he can't see the issue being resolved in any way other than by legislation or a referendum.
The Premier says he'll be getting more advice and talking to Queensland industry groups before finalising Queensland's position.
FERGUSON SAYS BUDGET STRATEGY NOT WORKING
Shadow Employment Minister, Martin Ferguson, says the Prime Minister must take responsibility for his budget mistakes, following today's figures showing unemployment has jumped to 8.6 percent.
Mr Ferguson says there are now 14 thousand fewer full time jobs than at the time of the August budget, and youth unemployment is at its highest for two-and-a-half years.
But Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer says the point two per cent rise in unemployment from November to December is just a hiccup in the statistics.
He says the government's well on its way to lowering the jobless rate and he's confident the Government's schemes to bolster small business are kicking-in, to create more jobs.
ROAD TOLL FIGURES DOWN
Figures out today show where were 1,973 deaths on Australian roads in 1996, a 2.2 per cent decline on 1995.
Federal Transport Minister John Sharp says the decrease is pleasing, but was only made possible by the vastly improved results in Queensland and New South Wales.
Mr Sharp's renewed his call for all states and territories to standardise road rules and penalties.
CALLS FOR VOYAGER CASE TO BE SETTLED OUT OF COURT
The Federal Government is being asked to settle out of court with a terminally ill survivor of the country's worst peace-time naval disaster.
The lawyer for 57 year old William McLean, has called for the Attorney General to facilitiate the settlement, saying his client has throat cancer and has only months to live.
Mr McLean was aboard HMAS Melbourne when it collided with HMAS Voyager in 1964.
He was originally awarded A$1.7 million in damages from the Commonwealth, which appealed the decision....with all funds being withheld until a retrial.
BOY GETS GOOD BEHAVIOUR BOND FOR OFFENCES
A ten-year-old Sydney boy has been given an 18-month good behaviour bond after pleading guilty to three of 20 charges.
The child, who obtained court permission to travel interstate with his social worker recently, pleaded guilty to three charges of stealing and breach of probation.
Magistrate Steve Scarlett sentenced the boy to 18-months probation and ordered him to attend school regularly and undergo counselling as directed.
Yesterday, the boy's lawyer told the court his client had spent his time in Queensland postively and the opportunity had not been a reward or a holiday at public expense.
The ten-year-old will be back in court in May after pleading not guilty to 17 separate charges.
MUSTER THROUGH TO THIRD ROUND
Fifth seed, Thomas Muster has won through to the third round of the Australian Open at Melbourne Park. Muster beat South African Grant Stafford in straight sets, 6-3, 6-2, 6-2.
Meanwhile, world number-one Pete Sampras has recovered from a slow start, to advance.
Sampras lost the first set and was down a break in the second against Adrian Voinea before fighting back to win in four, 3-6, 6-2, 6-3, 6-2.
He'll play Mark Woodforde who today breezed through to the third round in straight sets, against Argentina's Hernan Gumy.
Also through today, Scott Draper, 11th seed, Jim Courier, Martina Hingis, Anke Huber and Arantxa Sanchez-Vicario.
